items.summary: Nano24’s inhaled exosome therapy reduced respiratory failure in patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), hitting the main goal of a phase 2b study.

items.title: Pfizer makes ‘business decision’ to end phase 2 trial of autoimmune drug as program’s future uncertain
items.summary: Pfizer has called time on a phase 2 trial of its CXCR5 antibody in an autoimmune blood disorder, with the company tight-lipped on whether this marks the end of the road for the asset.

items.title: AstraZeneca taps Oracle to help improve recruitment for clinical trials
items.summary: AstraZeneca has turned to data giant Oracle as the U.K.-based Big Pharma works on one of the eternal problems of drug development—improving patient recruitment.

items.title: Ambrose Healthcare inks $181M deal for former Pfizer target AM-Pharma
items.summary: Ambrose Healthcare has bought AM-Pharma for up to 161 million euros, inking a cut-price deal for a biotech once courted by Pfizer.

items.title: Investment firm TCGX picks migraine biotech TriGemX to take public via SPAC
items.summary: Life sciences-focused investment firm TCGX will use a special purpose acquisition company to take migraine-minded TriGemX Bio public.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Layoff Tracker 2026: Enlivex excises 60%; Eyepoint halves headcount
items.summary: As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.

items.title: Lilly partners with Hong Kong's Metis in $1.1B deal to bolster AI nanoparticle discovery
items.summary: The collaboration is another in a series of partnerships Lilly has accumulated in both drug delivery and AI-based technologies.

items.title: Gilead ‘sitting on a foundational asset’ after oral UC drug's phase 2 win
items.summary: Gilead touted a mid-stage win for its inflammatory bowel disease pill after the treatment delivered clinical improvements in patients with ulcerative colitis.

items.title: Enlivex lays off 60% of employees, scraps preclinical R&D and gives execs ‘substantial’ salary cuts
items.summary: Enlivex is laying off 60% of its workforce, ending preclinical R&D and trimming its top execs’ salaries as the Israeli biotech tries to keep cash flowing to its osteoarthritis drug.

items.title: Merck KGaA buys Silence in $1.3B deal after siRNA drug's phase 2 blood cancer win
items.summary: Germany’s Merck KGaA has picked up Silence Therapeutics to the tune of $1.3 billion in the wake of the British biotech’s mid-stage success for its challenger to Takeda’s Mimrylo.

items.title: Disc spins past FDA rejection with ‘overwhelmingly positive’ phase 3 data for rare disease drug
items.summary: A phase 3 trial of Disc Medicine’s bitopertin has hit both co-primary endpoints and all secondary endpoints, positioning the biotech to refile for approval of the once-rejected rare disease drug candidate.

items.title: Siemens Healthineers partners with Paradromics to build out new imaging system to support BCIs
items.summary: Paradromics has announced a new collaboration with Siemens Healthineers to construct an advanced multimodal imaging platform to support the growing clinical use of implantable brain-computer interfaces (BCIs).

items.title: Alcon ponies up $550M for Neurotech, bagging approved cell therapy implant Encelto
items.summary: Eye specialty pharma Alcon has bought out Neurotech Pharmaceuticals for $550 million, gaining access to the approved Encelto and Neurotech's proprietary cell-based gene therapy delivery platform.

items.title: New US drug launches need price check to counter access impediments, ICER, West Health urge
items.summary: As policies from the last two presidential administrations put heightened focus on drug affordability in the United States, a new report suggests much work remains to be done when it comes to the launch prices of novel medicines.

items.title: CSL taps GSK’s Deborah Waterhouse as CEO in darkest hour
items.summary: Recruiting an industry veteran to steer the company through its darkest hour of growth pressures, CSL has hired GSK’s Deborah Waterhouse as its next CEO.

items.title: FDA solidifies stance on mobile apps, software used with prescription drugs in final guidance
items.summary: The agency clarified its framework for when drugmakers should include prescription drug apps in their labeling submissions or when app content should instead be treated as promotional material.

items.title: Regulatory tracker: Viatris' Ryzumvi wins FDA nod in age-related vision loss
items.summary: In this tracker, Fierce Pharma is recording the regulatory progress of in-market products, including expansions into key geographies and new indications. Some of these updates may not meet the bar for standalone stories, but we think they are still worth mentioning.

items.title: CDMO Samsung Bio wins temporary reprieve from strike threat after Seoul court ruling
items.summary: Ahead of a planned strike by its labor union later this month, Samsung Biologics has secured a favorable South Korean court ruling that shields most of its drug substance manufacturing operations from the labor action.

items.title: Antheia lands $80M conditional loan from Trump administration to onshore drug manufacturing
items.summary: The Department of War is allotting a conditional $80 million loan to next-gen ingredient maker Antheia, a move that will give the U.S. critical access to key starting materials and active pharmaceutical ingredients that are almost exclusively produced overseas.

items.title: Cosette lands FDA approval for Evoxac liquid in Sjögren’s disease
items.summary: The approval is for a liquid formulation of Evoxac, which was originally marketed by Daiichi Sankyo in capsules, providing an alternative treatment option for managing dry mouth symptoms in patients living with Sjögren’s disease.

items.title: AbbVie hits the gas on immunology awareness with McLaren F1 pact
items.summary: AbbVie has formed a multiyear deal with the McLaren Formula 1 team, signing up to raise awareness of immune-mediated diseases and provide funding for global charities.

items.title: Veradermics' hot streak continues with another phase 3 win in hair loss
items.summary: Topline results show the biotech's lead asset, VDPHL01, cleared all primary and secondary endpoints in a study of more than 500 men with mild-to-moderate pattern hair loss.

items.title: Amgen, AZ dive deep into Tezspire's Dupixent-challenging victory in EoE phase 3
items.summary: With little time elapsed since AstraZeneca and Amgen unveiled a topline win for Tezspire over the summer, the partners are upping the stakes with a detailed look at their inflammation-fighting antibody’s prowess in eosinophilic esophagitis.

items.title: GSK’s Jemperli scores FDA approval in rectal cancer, backed by high complete response rate
items.summary: Building on the buzz around a celebrated early trial readout, GSK’s Jemperli has earned a first-in-class FDA approval in a specific type of rectal cancer.

items.title: EyePoint cuts headcount, shifts priorities after another Duravyu AMD miss
items.summary: In new topline results, EyePoint disclosed that its tyrosine kinase inhibitor Duravyu performed worse than Eylea in patients with wet AMD, compelling the pharma to drop its program in the indication and make significant staff cuts.

items.title: Roche pauses future Germany investments, joining growing chorus of pharma pullbacks
items.summary: Amid tensions over government healthcare cost-cutting policies, Roche has slammed the brakes on new investments in Germany, joining an expanding group of drugmakers pulling back from the European country.

items.title: Novartis pauses midstage Fabhalta trial in lupus nephritis—but efficacy, safety not at play
items.summary: Amid a steady advance of kidney-focused label expansions, Novartis’ Fabhalta is slowing its roll in a key potential autoimmune niche.

items.title: The Next Chapter for AI in Clinical Trials
items.summary: As agentic AI enters clinical development, governance and human judgment will determine its value.

items.title: Eli Lilly's Omvoh takes phase 3 win in pediatric UC, fueling expansion ambitions
items.summary: A new positive phase 3 readout in kids with ulcerative colitis could help Lilly's Omvoh gain a competitive edge against its IL-23 rivals.

items.title: Closing the gap between approval and treatment
items.summary: Lauren Boyer, CEO of Underscore, on why patient finding is a marketing job, and how to reach the people traditional data can't see.

items.title: Why Are 53% of Phase 2 and 3 Trials Delayed? A Redesign Is Overdue
items.summary: A different model can improve quality, speed, and cost at once.

items.title: GSK taps actress Viola Davis for shingles-focused campaign
items.summary: The "How to Get Away With Murder" star is the face of GSK's "Shingles, actually" campaign, which positions an increased shingles risk as an untold reality of aging.

items.title: Trump's pharma holdings surged as drugmakers benefited from Medicare price negotiation carveouts, Democrats allege
items.summary: As midterms loom, Democrats on Congress’ Joint Economic Committee (JEC) are reviving concerns about the orphan drug carveout tucked into Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act, alleging that President Donald Trump accumulated millions of dollars in pharma stocks before and after the enactment of policies benefiting some of those same companies.

items.title: The Oral GLP-1 Tracker: Foundayo, Wegovy pill undergo minor fluctuations
items.summary: Fierce Pharma is launching the weekly Oral GLP-1 Tracker, leveraging analysts’ notes and IQVIA data to monitor prescription trends and shifting market shares as Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill and Eli Lilly's Foundayo vie to become the go-to oral weight-loss solution for millions.

items.title: Lilly's obesity pill, RevMed's pancreatic cancer breakthrough among slew of CHMP endorsements in Europe
items.summary: Across the pond, European regulators handed down a pair of pivotal approval recommendations this week, making way for a new front in Novo and Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 showdown and endorsing Revolution Medicines’ potential pancreatic cancer game changer.
